claims.text: Aluminum processed by ECAP for 4 passes using route Bc at approximately 150°C will have significantly greater ductility than conventionally annealed aluminum.
The initial material has a typical annealed aluminum microstructure.
Four ECAP passes via route Bc at approximately 150°C constitute the proposed processing intervention.
ECAP processing under the specified conditions will produce an ultra-fine-grained aluminum structure through severe plastic deformation.
Refined grains will enhance grain-boundary sliding in the processed aluminum.
Refined grains will promote a more uniform distribution of strain through increased dislocation motion.
Enhanced grain-boundary sliding and more uniform strain distribution will improve ductile behavior.
Ultra-fine-grained ECAP-processed aluminum will sustain more plastic deformation before fracture than annealed aluminum.
Conventionally annealed aluminum has larger grains than the proposed ECAP-processed aluminum.
Conventionally annealed aluminum has lower ductility than the proposed ECAP-processed aluminum.
The predicted ductility improvement is expected under standard ambient testing conditions.
The result may be specific to aluminum or similar highly malleable metals processed by ECAP.
